info.name: RepairFlow Backend
info.description:
Complete Postman collection for the current RepairFlow Sprint 1 backend. Covers health check, customer registration + email OTP + resend, customer login + OTP + resend, HttpOnly cookie session, refresh-token rotation, logout, protected /me, validation/security tests, and no-cookie/session checks.

IMPORTANT OTP TESTING:
1) Set testEmail to a real email address you can receive mail at.
2) POST /api/auth/register creates a REGISTER record in MongoDB collection `otp` and emails the same 6-digit code.
3) Copy that OTP into collection variable registrationOtp before Verify Registration OTP.
4) POST /api/auth/login creates a LOGIN record in `otp`; copy it into loginOtp before Verify Login OTP.
5) Resend endpoints have a default 60-second cooldown. Wait before running them.
6) Postman automatically maintains the HttpOnly cookies returned after login OTP verification.
7) Do not expect access/refresh tokens in the JSON body; they are intentionally stored as HttpOnly cookies.

item.name: Setup & Health

exec: pm.test('Service name is RepairFlow API', () => pm.expect(data.service).to.eql('RepairFlow API'));

request.description: Confirms that the RepairFlow API process is running.

item.description: Run this first after `npm run dev`.

item.name: Customer Registration

request.description: Creates or updates an UNVERIFIED customer and creates a REGISTER OTP in MongoDB collection `otp`. The same OTP is sent by email. Expected: 202. After this request, open MongoDB Atlas -> repairflow -> otp or check the email and copy the 6-digit code into collection variable `registrationOtp`.

Replaces the current REGISTER OTP with a new code in the separate `otp` collection and sends the new code by email. Default cooldown is 60 seconds. Wait until the cooldown has passed before running this request. Then update `registrationOtp` with the NEW code.
Verifies the REGISTER OTP from MongoDB/email. On success the OTP document is deleted and the user's `isEmailVerified` becomes true. Expected: 201.

item.description: Happy-path registration. If this email is already verified, change `testEmail` to another real address before rerunning.

item.name: Customer Login & Logout

request.description: Checks customer email/password first. If valid and registration is verified, creates a LOGIN OTP in `otp` and emails it. Expected: 202. Copy the LOGIN code into `loginOtp`.
Requires an existing pending LOGIN OTP. Default resend cooldown is 60 seconds. After success, replace `loginOtp` with the newly generated code.
Verifies the LOGIN OTP. On success the LOGIN OTP record is deleted, a server-side session is created, and access/refresh JWTs are returned only as HttpOnly cookies. Expected: 200.
Protected request. Postman should automatically send the access HttpOnly cookie set by Verify Login OTP.
Uses the HttpOnly refresh cookie. Rotates both refresh and access tokens and updates the stored refresh-token hash for the same server-side session. Expected: 200.

exec:
pm.test('Status is 200', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('User still authenticated', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().user.isEmailVerified).to.eql(true));

request.description: Confirms the newly rotated access-token cookie still authenticates correctly.

exec:
pm.test('Status is 200', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('Logout message is correct', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('Logged out successfully'));

request.description: Removes the current session from the user's activeSessions array and clears both auth cookies. Logout is idempotent. Expected: 200.
Confirms the session/cookies can no longer access a protected route after logout. Expected: 401.

item.description: Happy-path login plus complete JWT HttpOnly-cookie lifecycle.

item.name: Customer Forgot Password

request.description: Starts password recovery for a verified customer. Expected: 200. For account-enumeration protection, the response is generic. For a real verified customer, check email or MongoDB -> repairflow -> otp -> purpose FORGOT_PASSWORD, then copy the 6-digit OTP to collection variable `forgotPasswordOtp`.

Wait for OTP_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SECONDS (default 60 seconds) after the previous OTP send, then run this request. Expected after cooldown: 200. The old password-reset OTP is replaced. Copy the NEW OTP from email/MongoDB into `forgotPasswordOtp` before verifying.

Verifies the FORGOT_PASSWORD OTP. Expected: 200. The API returns a short-lived resetToken, and this request automatically saves it to the collection variable `resetToken`. The OTP document is deleted after successful verification.

Changes the password using the resetToken produced by the previous request. Expected: 200. Minimum password length is 12 characters. A successful reset revokes all existing customer sessions and makes the reset token unusable again.

item.description: Complete forgot-password flow. Use a verified customer account. OTP is stored in MongoDB `otp` collection with purpose `FORGOT_PASSWORD` and is also emailed. The verify request automatically saves the returned resetToken into the collection variable `resetToken`.

item.name: Owner Staff Setup

pm.test('Status is 202',()=>pm.response.to.have.status(202));
const d=pm.response.json(); pm.test('Role is owner_staff',()=>pm.expect(d.account.role).to.eql('owner_staff')); pm.test('OTP required',()=>pm.expect(d.requiresOtp).to.eql(true));

request.description: Requires header x-owner-setup-key. Creates the only owner_staff account as pending and emails an OTP.
Wait for the OTP cooldown, then replace ownerSetupOtp with the NEW code from email/MongoDB.
Activates the one Owner/Staff account.

item.description: Run Owner/Staff Setup only once on a fresh database. After the first setup request creates the pending owner_staff account, use resend/verify; a second setup request is rejected. Login and session tokens use HttpOnly cookies.
